newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 B share results indicate polarisation.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 B share results indicate polarisation.

text.p: The overall profitability of China's foreign currency B share companies appears to have shrunk in 1996 for the third year in a row, but 1997 is likely to be the year of the turnaround, analysts said on Tuesday.
Almost all of China's 87 B share firms have now posted their 1996 results, ahead of the Wednesday deadline, with Shenzhen companies generally performing better than Shanghai's.
"I think the worst is over," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage in Shanghai. "Even with the worst of the companies, this is probably a buying opportunity. They can only get better."
He said it was his impression that results overall for Shanghai were down 10 to 20 percent over 1995.

The worst performers included such companies as textile machinery maker Shanghai Erfangji which reported a net profit fall of 93.24 percent to just 1.223 million yuan compared to 18.089 million in 1995.
Glass maker Shanghai Yaohua saw profits plunge 56.85 percent to 113.563 million from 263.193 million in 1995.
"There is a trend of polarisation in the 1996 annual results by the B share firms," said one Shenzhen-based stock analyst with China Guotai Securities.

"New firms listed since the start of 1996 have posted strong results while some old poor firms, which listed shares in the first couple of years after the B share markets were set up in 1992, have become even worse," he said.
Analysts said a better performance overall of the Shenzhen-listed stocks could help the Shenzhen market to continue to rise.

"The (Shenzhen) B share market is accumulating momentum to test the 200-point level next month after the end of the 1996 annual reporting season," a Shenzhen-based analyst with China Southern Securities said.
"Many investors believe listed companies are likely to show some improvement in their 1997 interim earnings due to China's improving economy," he said.

Shanghai's B share index has gained around 30 percent from the start of 1996 and its Shenzhen counterpart is up by 20 percent on a bull run based largely on optimism about the improving fundamentals of China's economy in 1997, analysts said.
Further rises could occur in July or August when the firms are expected to post much better interim results for 1997 against 1996, they said.
With the 1996 results mostly in, many brokers said their recommended "buys" included portable phone maker Eastern Communications Co, Dazhong Taxi Co and Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co
In Shenzhen, they included washing-machine marker Wuxi Little Swan Co, Guangdong Electric Power Development Co, diesel engine maker Changchai Co and colour TV tube producer Shenzhen SEG Co.
